question: Sara purchased 30 kg of sugar at 60 per kg and another 20 kg of sugar at 70 per kg. She combined both quantities and then sold the entire mixture at 68 per kg What was her total profit or loss?
solution:
**Given:**

Quantity of sugar purchased at ₹60 per kg = 30 kg

Quantity of sugar purchased at ₹70 per kg = 20 kg

Combined selling price of the mixture = ₹68 per kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost Price = (Quantity₁ × Price₁) + (Quantity₂ × Price₂)

Total Selling Price = Combined Quantity × Selling Price per kg

Profit/Loss = Total Selling Price − Total Cost Price

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Cost Price = (30 × 60) + (20 × 70)

⇒ Total Cost Price = 1800 + 1400

⇒ Total Cost Price = ₹3200

⇒ Total Selling Price = (30 + 20) × 68

⇒ Total Selling Price = 50 × 68

⇒ Total Selling Price = ₹3400

⇒ Profit = Total Selling Price − Total Cost Price

⇒ Profit = 3400 − 3200

⇒ Profit = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 200.**
